state.misconception_label: Thinks you can find missing values in a given table by treating the row as linear and adding on the difference between the first two values given.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: The equation \( f=3 r^{2}+3 \) is used to find values in the table below. What is the value covered by the star? \begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline\( r \) & \( 1 \) & \( 2 \) & \( 3 \) & \( 4 \) \\ \hline\( f \) & \( 6 \) & \( 15 \) & \( \color{gold}\bigstar \) & \\ \hline \end{tabular}. I got \( 24 \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Why did you choose to add on the difference between the first two values to find the missing value in the table? Can you think of any other ways to approach this problem that might lead to a different result?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I thought that since the numbers were going up, I could just keep adding the difference like it was a straight line. But now I'm not sure if that's the right way to do it. How do I actually use the equation to find the missing value?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you think of how the equation \( f=3 r^{2}+3 \) relates to the values in the table? How might you use the equation to find the value covered by the star in a different way than simply adding on the difference between the first two values?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I guess I should use the equation \( f=3 r^{2}+3 \) to find the missing value instead of just adding the differences. So, for \( r=3 \), I would plug it into the equation, right? But I'm not totally sure how to do that. Can you help me figure out what \( f \) would be when \( r=3 \)?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher explicitly addresses the linear addition misconception and guides the student to recognize they should use the quadratic equation instead, though by Turn 4 the student still needs help with basic substitution, suggesting the scaffolding could have been more precisely calibrated to their actual skill level.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses probing questions to guide the student toward recognizing their flawed reasoning (assuming linear growth) and discovering the correct approach (using the equation), without ever directly providing the answer or method.
